proposed_local_additions.statement: A based loop in a C² surface is based-homotopic to a regular C² immersed loop having only finitely many transverse double points and no triple points; all construction choices are finite or countable.
proposed_local_additions.title: Finite general position for a leafwise loop
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Cover the compact original loop by finitely many coordinate disks and subdivide its parameter circle so successive pieces lie in these disks. Replace each piece by a finite coordinate-polygonal path with the same endpoints; convex coordinate homotopies give the specified homotopy. Perturb the finitely many vertices and directions to remove constant pieces and retracing adjacent tangents, keeping the basepoint fixed. Round corners in disjoint source intervals using coordinate convolution and a cutoff on straight tails. One coordinate remains strictly increasing across each rounded corner, so the curve is regular. This yields a regular C² curve; compactness gives a uniform source neighborhood of the diagonal on which no two distinct parameters have equal images.

For source pairs outside that neighborhood, choose a finite product-box cover, each pair of disjoint source intervals mapping into one surface coordinate disk whenever their images can coincide. Use finitely many C² bump perturbations supported in these source intervals, with two independent coordinate displacement parameters on each smaller interval. At any equality of two branches, the parameter derivative of their coordinate difference has rank2. The universal equality set is thus a C² manifold; projection to the finite parameter space has equal source and target dimensions. Sard’s equal-dimensional clause makes its critical values null; choose a parameter outside the finitely many critical-value sets. At that parameter every double point is transverse. The same independent branch parameters make the triple-equality set have source dimension one less than parameter dimension, so Sard excludes all triple points. Work on the finitely many compact pair/triple boxes; if smaller open cores are required, use a fixed countable rational exhaustion and avoid the resulting countable union of null sets. This uses at most ACω, not a family of choices indexed by all curve points. The transverse double-pair set is compact (away from the excluded diagonal neighborhood) and discrete, hence finite. Small perturbations preserve regularity and the based homotopy by the coordinate straight-line homotopies. The only prescribed basepoint can be retained, and generic directions of other branches avoid it.

proposed_local_additions.statement: Every compact subset of a C² surface lies in the interior of a compact finitely cellulated subsurface. Finite orientable polygon reduction gives closed surface genus normal forms, free groups for nonempty-boundary surfaces, torsion-free surface groups, and an embedded disk bounded by any embedded null curve (unique unless the entire leaf is a sphere). These clauses need only ACω.
proposed_local_additions.title: Finite surface normal forms, Jordan disks, and torsion control
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
For a compact set K choose finitely many relatively compact surface charts covering it and finitely many C² coordinate bump functions whose sum f exceeds1 on K and has compact support. Sard for the C² scalar f gives a regular a∈(0,1). The union of the components of {f≥a} meeting K is a compact subsurface S with C² boundary and K in its interior; it has finitely many components because its compact regular boundary and compact manifold chart cover give finite component charts. In a noncompact connected surface, a connected component containing connected K has nonempty boundary: an empty-boundary compact codimension-zero region would be open and closed and equal the whole surface.

Construct a finite cellulation of S without using arbitrary Jordan curves. Choose finitely many coordinate disks with smaller cores covering S. Move their radii generically so their boundary circles and ∂S intersect transversely, with no triple points; the C² scalar Sard clause on each of the finitely many prior arcs supplies these radii. Add all finitely many crossings as graph vertices. Each arrangement face has constant membership in every disk, hence lies in one disk whose core-cover point it contains. Within that coordinate disk, straighten finite regular arcs near their vertices and replace each compact regular edge by a close polygonal edge inside its disjoint thin strip. Compact inverse-function neighborhoods ensure the replacement is a graph over the old edge, so stripwise interpolation is an ambient isotopy. For an isolated closed regular curve, its short normal collar is injective by compactness and IFT; a sufficiently fine inscribed polygon is a graph in that collar and isotopic to it. Thus only the choice-free polygonal Jordan theorem is required. Add finite planar crosscuts between distinct boundary components of an arrangement face, then triangulate its simple polygonal faces by ears. Reconcile the finite subdivisions on shared edges. Reversing the strip isotopies gives a finite curvilinear triangular cellulation of S. This is the finite supplied-chart part of the published curvilinear construction, with its full-AC arbitrary-Jordan input replaced by the regular-curve polygon argument just given.

Cut a spanning tree of the finite primal graph and a spanning tree of the dual graph to obtain one finite polygon schema (published one-polygon lemma, proof steps1.1–3.1). All orientable paired sides occur with opposite traversal signs. The finite schema moves cancel adjacent aa^{-1}; an interlaced pair a,b is cut and pasted into one handle block aba^{-1}b^{-1}, which is set aside. If no pair interlaces, an innermost adjacent inverse pair exists and cancels. Each operation deletes a pair or sets aside a block, so finite side count decreases. Unpaired boundary circles remain boundary circles. The result is genus g with b boundary circles, χ=2−2g−b; for b>0, the standard polygon edge retraction gives the free group on 2g+b−1 generators. These are the finite operations in the published polygonal reduction-moves item, not its full-AC triangulation-existence premise. For b=0 the same schema gives sphere for g=0, torus for g=1, and the usual oriented genus-g model; χ=0 identifies exactly the torus. Finite regular chart and collar smoothing makes the model maps C² diffeomorphisms in the present C² category.

Torsion-freeness is local to a compact subsurface: a loop and a null cap of its m-th power have compact connected image K, so lie in such an S. With boundary, π₁(S) is free and cyclic reduction of a nonempty reduced word shows its positive powers stay nonempty. For closed S, genus0 has trivial group and genus1 has Z². For genus≥2 split off one handle: van Kampen writes the group as an amalgam of two free groups over the infinite cyclic boundary subgroup. The boundary word is a nonempty cyclically reduced product of commutators in each free factor, so those edge injections are injective. The published amalgam normal-form theorem then makes any finite-order element conjugate into a factor: an alternating cyclically reduced word has powers of strictly increasing syllable length. Thus no torsion exists. Its coset data require no full AC here: free groups have explicit finite-word enumerations, and one chooses the first word in each cyclic coset.

Finally take an embedded null curve c and its compact null cap, include them in S and cellulate with c as a subgraph by the same finite regular arrangement. If c is nonseparating, a crossing dual curve gives algebraic intersection1, so c is not null. If it separates and neither side is a disk, their boundary subgroup generated by c injects in each side: the finite polygon word is nonempty in each non-disk oriented boundary surface. Van Kampen and amalgam normal form would then make c nontrivial in S, contradicting the supplied null cap. Hence one side is a disk, embedded in S and therefore in the original surface. If both sides are disks their union is an open-and-closed sphere surface; otherwise the disk is unique. The same argument applies to a simply connected leaf cover without identifying it globally with the plane.

proposed_local_additions.statement: For a compact C² oriented region W in a closed oriented smooth three-manifold, with oriented C¹ plane bundle E tangent to every boundary component and one common inward transverse direction, the finite sum of boundary Euler characteristics is zero. For a finitely cellulated compact oriented surface, a tangent section with isolated nondegenerate zeros has total index V−E+F.
proposed_local_additions.title: Finite tangent index count and inward boundary sum
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
First prove the finite surface index clause. The finite cellulation gives a handle layout consisting of one small disk for each vertex, one rectangular band for each edge, and one filling disk for each face. Build a tangent section with one radial source (+1) in each vertex disk, one linear saddle (−1) in each edge band, and one radial sink (+1) in each face disk. Match its nonzero directions on the product collars of adjacent handles; finite bump interpolation between vectors in a common open half-plane introduces no zero. Thus its index sum is V−E+F. To compare any other tangent section with finitely many nondegenerate zeros, join them by a section homotopy and perturb it generically relative its two ends. Its zero set in the surface×[0,1] is an oriented compact1-manifold, so the two end index sums agree by finite interval boundary cancellation. Genericity is obtained with finitely many frame bumps whose parameter derivatives span each fiber; Sard applies to the parameter projection, whose source dimension exceeds target dimension by1 and whose regularity is C². At the ends the local zero orientation is the sign of the invertible derivative, the usual index. Small smoothing/perturbation preserves these isolated indices.

For the three-dimensional boundary sum, avoid requiring a finite CW decomposition of W or a general Thom class. Choose one smooth transverse field V near W. Smoothly approximate a C¹ cooriented annihilator for E using finite coordinate convolutions and bumps, obtaining a smooth1-form ω′ with ω′(V)>0. Its kernel E′ is a smooth oriented rank2 subbundle. Projection along V gives an oriented C¹ bundle isomorphism E→E′. Choose a generic smooth section s of E′ near W, using finitely many local frame bumps spanning each fiber on compact W. The universal section map is a submersion in these finite parameters. Sard for the interior projection (smooth) and for its C² boundary restriction (dimension excess1) gives parameters for which s is transverse to0 on W and on ∂W. Its zero set is consequently a compact oriented1-manifold with boundary, and the signed sum of its boundary points is0. No countable or uncountable family of frame selections is used after the finite cover.

Pull its boundary restriction back through E→E′ to a tangent section on each boundary surface. This is C¹ and has isolated nondegenerate zeros; its indices equal those of the E′ section because the bundle isomorphism preserves orientation. If a C² homotopy is needed for the comparison above, approximate in the smooth E′ bundle on the C² boundary using finitely many chart convolutions; sufficiently small C¹ approximation preserves the nondegenerate zeros and indices. The finite surface clause identifies each component’s index sum with its finite χ=V−E+F. The ambient and plane orientations together orient the zero curves. Since the chosen transverse V points inward on EVERY boundary component, their induced boundary sign is the same negative of the tangent-section index on each component. Thus 0=−Σ_C χ(C). This is the needed finite tangent-Euler boundary-sum calculation established directly by zero curves, without assuming a full-AC Thom theorem or an unproved e_fin comparison. The finite cell counts equal homological χ by the published finite-CW Euler–Poincare theorem.

proposed_local_additions.statement: For a generic finite-double-point representative of a nonzero Π class, a sufficiently short one-field leaf-synchronized fence exists, compact leafwise sets separate from short nonzero flow displacements, and all level intersections use one fixed finite crossing word with a strictly decreasing subword-cut rank.
proposed_local_additions.title: Fixed transverse fences and their finite crossing words
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Let K be the image of a compact intrinsic subset of a leaf, and V a smooth transverse vector field. There is η>0 such that φ_s(K)∩K is empty for 0<|s|<η. Cover K by finitely many intrinsic neighborhoods each contained in one plaque of a box. On pairs in the same such neighborhood, the transverse coordinate strictly changes along V, uniformly for short time. The complement of their union in K×K is compact and has no diagonal; continuity of the flow and the closed ambient diagonal give one short interval of inequality on that complement. Take the minimum. The same proof handles finitely many compact sets in distinct leaves by their disjoint intrinsic union.

Choose a smooth positive transverse field V near the compact loop by a finite positive combination of constant chart vectors. Cover the loop by finitely many boxes. In each box the V-flow lines are transverse, so the implicit function theorem identifies each nearby plaque with a graph over a small piece of the original loop using V-orbit projection. Successive plaque continuations starting at φ_t(f(0)) agree on overlaps by uniqueness of plaque transport. Finite subdivision gives a C² family F(u,t)=φ_{τ(u,t)}(f(u)) with τ(u,0)=0 and τ_t>0. The return time is the one-sided holonomy map on the base V-orbit. Because [f] is in N_j its germ is identity, so shrinking t gives F(0,t)=F(1,t) and a periodic time function τ. By the existing finite-chart fence-independence argument for Q_j, these closed loops are null on every positive sufficiently small level. This construction uses one fixed V throughout; arbitrary point tracks cannot be substituted in the next lemma. The regularity assertion uses C² box coordinates and the C² implicit function theorem for intersection with a V-orbit, not a C²-dependence claim for an arbitrary C¹ ODE.

Given a C² immersed generic loop f:S¹→L with N transverse double points and no triple points, choose its fixed-V fence F and shrink it so 0≤τ(u,t)<η/3, where η is the compact separation bound for K=f(S¹). If F(u,t)=F(v,t), flow uniqueness gives φ_{τ(u,t)-τ(v,t)}(f(u))=f(v). Separation forces τ(u,t)=τ(v,t), and then f(u)=f(v). Hence every double point at every level uses one of the same N fixed parameter pairs (u_i,v_i). The equality need not hold for all levels: it is used only where it actually holds. Shrink once more so regularity and nonparallel tangents at all possible double points persist. At a possible crossing the common flow time is the same; the tangential vectors are the original nonparallel vectors acted on by Dφ, with small transverse corrections imposed by leafwise tangency, so nonparallelness follows from compact C¹ control.

View f as a finite cyclic word of arcs by marking the 2N crossing preimages. A reduced word traverses some of these arcs, each at most once, with switches only at marked pairs. A selected crossing is a vertex visited twice; cutting there gives two cyclic subwords, each visiting that vertex only once. Neither new word can reintroduce a deleted arc or a second visit at a vertex already used for a switch. Define r(w) to be the number of original vertices visited twice by w, counting a switch vertex once (its two end representatives are one visit). Then each cut word has r≤r(w)−1. All possible non-endpoint collisions of any level of any reduced word are at vertices counted by r(w); absence of new intersections follows from the preceding flow-separation argument. This ranking is fixed by the original loop and is uniform over all lower parameters, even when closedness sets have many components.

proposed_local_additions.statement: Finite transversal control: (i) an intrinsically noncompact leaf in compact M meets a C² positive closed immersed transversal; (ii) saturation of a transversal is open; (iii) a compact nearby leaf through a sufficiently small base parameter of a compact leaf is a one-sheeted collar graph, preserving essential transported loops.
proposed_local_additions.title: Finite transversal control and compact collar graphs
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
## Lemma B: a noncompact leaf meets a closed transversal

**Contract.** Assume ACω. Let F be a C² cooriented codimension-one foliation of a compact boundaryless smooth manifold M, and L an intrinsically noncompact leaf. Then there is a positively transverse C² immersed circle meeting L. No embeddedness or arbitrary-neighborhood clause is asserted.

**Proof, finite plaque detection.** Choose finitely many C² foliation boxes U_i with coordinates `(-2,2)^(n−1)×(-2,2)`, whose smaller open cores V_i, coordinates `(-1,1)^(n−1)×(-1,1)`, cover M. If L met each V_i in only finitely many U_i-plaques, then the finitely many corresponding compact plaque squares `[-1,1]^(n−1)×{r}` would be intrinsically compact subsets of L whose union contains L. Their union would equal L and make it compact. Hence one V_i meets infinitely many plaques of L. In particular, on its central vertical interval choose two distinct plaque points x=(0,r_x) and y=(0,r_y) of L with r_x<r_y.

**Proof, positive perturbation of the leaf path.** Connectedness of L and its local Euclidean charts give a finite piecewise C² leafwise path from y to x. Smooth its finitely many corners intrinsically in convex leaf charts, giving a C² path γ:[0,1]→L with γ(0)=y and γ(1)=x. It may have stationary points; regularity of γ is unnecessary. Such corner smoothing uses finite local interpolation, not manifold-valued Whitney approximation.

Construct ω and X near the compact path as described above, with smooth local flow φ. For small a≥0 put `v(s,a)=ω_(φ_a(γ(s)))(Dφ_a(γ′(s)))`. Since γ is leafwise, v(s,0)=0. The C¹ form, smooth flow and compact parameter domain imply uniform bounds `|v(s,a)|≤A a` and `ω(X)≥b>0` there. Indeed ∂_a v is continuous on a fixed compact neighborhood, so the ordinary mean-value estimate gives A.

Choose B>A/b and δ>0, and set `a(s)=δ(e^(Bs)−1)/B`. Then a(0)=0, a′=Ba+δ. For δ small, the path `γ_δ(s)=φ_(a(s))(γ(s))` is defined and C², and
`ω(γ_δ′) = v(s,a(s))+a′(s)ω(X) ≥ −Aa+b(Ba+δ)>0`.
Thus it is positively transverse, starting at y and ending at x_δ near x. In the original box, the transverse coordinate of x_δ is strictly above r_x, because X is positive there; make δ so small that it remains below r_y and the tangential coordinates stay in the core. The straight box-coordinate segment from x_δ to y lies in that core and has strictly increasing transverse coordinate. Its image under the C² chart inverse is positively transverse. Together these paths form a closed piecewise C² positive transverse curve.

**Proof, seam smoothing and intersection.** At each of its two joins, take a small foliation box and a parameter interval on which both one-sided transverse-coordinate derivatives have a common positive lower bound c. In chart coordinates mollify the continuous piecewise C² curve with a nonnegative smooth kernel. The mollified transverse derivative is an average of derivatives and remains ≥c. Blend the original curve and its mollification using a smooth cutoff equal to one near the join and zero outside the chosen interval. The added transverse derivative is the cutoff derivative times the difference of the transverse coordinates, which tends uniformly to zero with mollifier radius. Choose the radius so its absolute value is <c/2. The resulting chart curve is C², still positively transverse, and equals the old curve on open end collars; finite gluing gives a C² immersed circle.

At the join y, before smoothing the incoming transverse coordinate lies below r_y and the outgoing one lies above r_y. Keep those interval endpoints fixed. After smoothing the coordinate remains strictly increasing and crosses r_y by the intermediate value theorem. Its crossing point lies in the local plaque through y, hence in L. Therefore the smoothed closed transversal still meets L. ∎

This supplies a precise C²/ACω version of Novikov §1 Lemma1.2, printed p.3, without his “obvious approximation.” Batch22 already has `lem-a-non-closed-leaf-of-a-codimension-one-foliation-meets-a-closed-transversal`, but that statement concerns a leaf **not closed as an ambient subset**, outputs an embedded circle, and is in the smooth setting. It cannot silently be substituted for this intrinsic-noncompact/C² contract. The draft deliberately proves only the immersed closed-transversal conclusion needed here.



Saturation is open: join any leaf point to a crossing by a finite leafwise path. Finite box transport carries a small open transversal interval to one through that point, and the terminal union of plaques is an open neighborhood all of whose leaves meet the original transversal. Taking the union over eligible paths requires no selection of one path per point.

Use a finite foliation-box cover of L and a finite system of connecting paths and generating loops for π₁(L). Compactness permits shrinking the base transversal so all generator holonomy maps H_i and their inverses are defined on [0,ε], and the finitely many chart and connecting-path transports stay in a fixed tubular collar. All H_i are increasing and fix0. If B meets the base transversal at t, then H_i(t) and every defined iterate belong to B. If H_i(t)<t, its forward iterates form a strictly decreasing sequence in [0,t], converging to some fixed a≥0; if H_i(t)>t, use inverse iterates, again decreasing in [0,t]. The iterations remain defined in the common small domain. B is compact intrinsically, so its inclusion is an ambient embedding and closed; the limit transversal point belongs to B. A transverse interval meets an embedded leaf locally in an isolated point, contradicting the infinitely many distinct iterates converging to a. Hence H_i(t)=t for every generator.

For the graph conclusion, choose finitely many local plaques along a finite tree of connecting paths from the basepoint to the finite covering boxes. Continue the plaque through t along each tree path; this gives a finite collection of local sections over L, contained in the collar after the uniform shrink. On overlaps the difference of paths is a based loop. Express that loop in the finite generator system. Its holonomy at t fixes t because each generator and inverse does. Ensure the finitely many overlap path relations are valid on the chosen common transversal by finite subdivision of their compact homotopies into boxes, and shrink once more using only these finitely many relations. Thus the local sections agree on overlaps. They patch to a C² graph s_t:L→M, whose image is contained in the leaf B and is compact. Projection along the collar restricts to its inverse, so it is an embedding. Its image is open in B by the leafwise inverse function theorem and closed in B by intrinsic compactness; connectedness makes it all of B. The graph is therefore diffeomorphic to L. A transported loop projects to the original loop, so if it were null in B its projected nullhomotopy would null the original loop in L, proving essentiality.

The finite generator and finite-chart-tree system can be constructed from a finite cellulation of the compact surface L. This proof uses no finite-holonomy Reeb-stability theorem and asserts no product neighborhood for all nearby leaves. It only identifies the nearby leaves that are themselves compact.

proposed_local_additions.title: Closed null fence words have essential lower endpoints
proposed_local_additions.strategy: For a piecewise C² path following a fixed finite V-fence word, suppose at parameter r it is closed and has a compact nullhomotopy in its leaf. Finite subdivision of that compact cap into foliation boxes transports the cap over a uniform two-sided interval around r. On each boundary segment its transported path equals the prescribed word by uniqueness of plaque transport from the same initial V-orbit. In particular the ending point equals the initial point, since the cap boundary closes, and the word remains null. Thus its closed-and-null parameter set U is relatively open. Its closed parameter set E is closed because both endpoint tracks are continuous and M is Hausdorff. This does not assert U is closed. At a lower endpoint a of a component (a,r] of U, endpoint continuity makes the word closed; if the word were null at a, the same finite cap argument would extend U below a. Hence the word is essential at a (unless the component already includes the initial parameter).

proposed_local_additions.statement: For the present closed connected smooth three-manifold with C² cooriented foliation, one compact sphere leaf forces every leaf to be a compact sphere. Consequently a nonzero Π leaf excludes every spherical leaf and every sphere universal-cover alternative.
proposed_local_additions.title: Spherical stability at C² and countable-choice strength
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Local spherical stability is finite: cover a compact sphere by finitely many foliation boxes, choose finitely many connecting paths and finite overlap relations. Every based loop is contractible, so finite compact homotopy transport makes all these overlap transports identity on one common short transversal. They patch to a compact plaque graph for every sufficiently small transverse parameter, giving a saturated product sphere neighborhood. Therefore the union S of spherical leaves is nonempty, open and saturated.

The rational homology of the compact smooth ambient M is finite-dimensional without full AC. Choose a smooth metric by finite chart bumps. Local exponential-map IFT and the positive quadratic Hessian of squared distance, with uniform finite-chart bounds after shrinking, provide sufficiently small strongly convex balls with unique short minimizing geodesics. Take the collection of ALL such small balls; it covers M, and compactness selects finitely many. Shrink their uniform radius below the finite injectivity bound, so any nonempty finite intersection is geodesically convex: its two points have one common short geodesic, contained in each ball. Each intersection contracts to one of its points along these geodesics. Mayer–Vietoris, inducting on the finite number of cover sets and then on their finite intersection covers, shows that every H_k(M;Q) is finite-dimensional. This uses no choice of balls at every point and no unproved full-AC finite-CW theorem.

Let x∈closure(S), with leaf A. If A were intrinsically noncompact, for every finite collection of spherical leaves B₁,…,B_n construct a positive closed transversal through A avoiding that collection. This is the intrinsic-noncompact transversal construction with finite compact barriers: refine a finite ambient box cover so each selected compact embedded B_i has only its finitely many local plaques; an infinite-plaque A-box has infinitely many A plaques in one of the finitely many transverse intervals cut by these B_i plaques. Choose two there, join them by a finite path in A, positively perturb that path in the complement of the compact B_i union, and close by a positive vertical segment inside the same interval. Finite smoothing preserves the avoidance and positivity. Saturation of the resulting transversal is open and contains A, hence contains x and some spherical leaf B arbitrarily near x. This new B meets the transversal, while every chosen B_i misses it.

Oriented transverse intersection gives [B] outside the rational span of [B_i]: all intersections with B have one strict sign, whereas all intersections with B_i are absent. This is the finite compact intersection clause: subdivide a finite bounding chain into transverse chart pieces, and cancel paired internal faces to see a closed transversal has zero algebraic pairing with any rational boundary; therefore the nonzero intersection detects nonzero quotient homology. C² leaves suffice for this finite local perturbation and orientation count. Applying this to a finite basis of the span of ALL spherical-leaf classes contradicts the finite-dimensional H₂(M;Q). Thus A is compact.

Now apply the compact-nearby-leaf graph lemma to compact A. Spherical leaves B arbitrarily close through the chosen base transversal are compact, so their finite generator holonomies fix that parameter, and they are one-sheeted compact graphs over A. Hence A is diffeomorphic to B=S². This proves closure(S)⊂S without the false assertion that a connected saturated Hausdorff limit is one leaf. S is open, closed, nonempty, so connectedness gives S=M. All sphere-leaf fundamental groups are trivial, and therefore all Π groups are zero. Finally a compact simply connected oriented surface cover is a sphere by the finite surface normal form; its covered oriented leaf is also sphere (finite covering of a compact simply connected sphere has no nontrivial free orientation-preserving deck group, or use the finite Euler covering count). Thus the sphere-cover alternative is excluded in the nonzeroΠ application.

For completeness all leaves also meet a positive closed transversal when S=M. Their finite product neighborhoods are saturated, and any two distinct compact leaves have disjoint sufficiently small such neighborhoods; thus the quotient is Hausdorff. It is a compact connected cooriented1-manifold without boundary, covered by finitely many interval charts, so elementary finite interval gluing identifies it with a circle. These product charts make M a sphere bundle over that circle. Lift its one circuit to a product over [0,1] with endpoint monodromy f. A finite C² path in the connected sphere fiber from x to f^{-1}(x), constant on end collars, gives a section whose endpoint gluing agrees; its projection travels positively once around the circle, so it is a positive closed transversal. This finite construction supplies the no-transversal contradiction if spherical leaves are invoked without a separate nonzeroΠ assumption. For a compact simply connected oriented covering surface, compact-to-Hausdorff and discrete fibers give a finite cover of its leaf. Lift a finite base triangulation to count χ(cover)=dχ(leaf). The cover has χ=2; orientable finite normal forms give χ(leaf)=2−2g, so2=d(2−2g) forces g=0 and d=1. Thus a sphere universal cover means an actual sphere leaf, without a finite-group plane-action theorem.

proposed_local_additions.statement: From a nonzero Π^j class represented by a generic finite-crossing loop, at every sufficiently small upper height one obtains after at most N subword cuts an essential lower loop with a coherent genuinely closed/null right family whose lifts are simple at EVERY positive parameter.
proposed_local_additions.title: Finite compatible reduction of an arbitrary Π fence
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Begin with an essential loop at parameter a₀=0 and a closed/null family on (0,b], represented by the full cyclic word w₀. If every positive level has a simple lift to its leaf universal cover, stop. Otherwise choose one positive r≤b at which the lift has a selfintersection. The corresponding marked pair cuts the word into two loops c_t,d_t. At r both are closed and null: each is the projection of a closed subpath of the closed lifted loop, and the universal cover is simply connected. By finite compact-cap persistence both are closed/null on a neighborhood of r. Let (a,r] be the maximal common downward interval on which both are closed/null, relative to the current fence interval [a₀,r]. At a both loops are closed by continuity. If a>a₀ and both were null there, compact-cap persistence for both would extend the interval below a, contradiction. If a=a₀ and both were null, their product would make the current initial essential loop null, contradiction. Thus at least one factor is essential at a. Choose it, retain only the family on [a,r], and rebase and rescale. The new initial leaf need not be the old one; the family stays on the same chosen transverse side and every positive displacement is genuinely closed and null. The rank of its cyclic word is strictly smaller by the preceding lemma. Repeat only when an actual positive-level lift is nonsimple. There are at most N such operations. At termination ALL positive lifts are simple, since otherwise another rank-decreasing operation would be possible. The initial parameter belongs to [0,b), so choosing b arbitrarily small makes the reduced essential initial leaf arbitrarily close to L. No cut is projected below its common closed/null interval, and no claim about closedness of nullness is used.

The result is the finite reduction and simple lifted boundary part of Novikov Lemma7.2. Obtaining regular disk fillings from those simple lifts additionally uses the oriented simply connected surface/Jordan-disk supplier (sphere alternative included); the reduction does not identify a changing universal cover with ℝ². The source's sphere exclusion and coherent disk continuation are separate next steps.

proposed_local_additions.statement: If a leaf L of a compact cooriented C² foliation meets no closed transversal, its strict positive accessible set N has compact C² manifold closure W with finitely many compact boundary leaves, including L, and positive normals point inward everywhere on ∂W.
proposed_local_additions.title: A no-transversal leaf bounds a finite inward accessibility region
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Let N consist of endpoints of actual positive transverse paths beginning on L. Finite box endpoint perturbations and finite leafwise path transport make N open and saturated. It excludes L, because a positive path from L to L can be closed by the finite endpoint-alignment and positive smoothing construction to give a forbidden closed transversal. Short positive segments at every point of L show L⊂closure(N), hence L⊂∂N.

In a cooriented box, membership in the saturated set N depends only on the transverse coordinate z. If z∈N and z<z′ in that box, append the positive vertical segment to reach z′, so z′∈N. Consequently the transverse-coordinate membership set is an open upward interval: empty, all, or (a,upper). Around each boundary point it has exactly the latter form. Therefore ∂N is locally one whole plaque and closure(N) is locally the positive half-box. The boundary height is constant within its plaque box, so these are C² manifold-with-boundary charts for W=closure(N). Compactness of M gives compact W and a finite boundary box cover. Each boundary box contains just one boundary plaque; hence only finitely many boundary leaves occur, since distinct leaves have disjoint plaques.

Each boundary leaf C avoids closed transversals. Otherwise the saturation of a closed positive transversal through C is open and contains C; because C⊂closure(N), this saturation meets N. Thus some reachable leaf D also meets that same transversal. Following its positive orientation from a D-crossing to a C-crossing (going once around if needed) makes C reachable from D and hence from L. This contradicts C⊂∂N and C∩N empty. The intrinsic-noncompact-leaf transversal lemma then makes every boundary leaf compact. Equivalently, local one-plaque boundary charts and their finite compact plaque cores give a finite intrinsic compact covering. The positive normal direction points into N at every boundary point by the upward interval description. This is the strict accessible REGION of L; it is not automatically a mutual-accessibility class or the Π-side Reeb component.

proposed_local_additions.statement: With the finite plane-bundle Euler boundary-sum carrier and oriented compact-surface normal forms, every no-closed-transversal leaf of the present closed oriented cooriented three-manifold foliation is a torus.
proposed_local_additions.title: A no-transversal Π leaf is a torus
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Construct W and its finitely many compact boundary leaves C_i by the preceding local geometric proof. The oriented plane bundle TF extends over W and restricts on each C_i to TC_i. The ambient orientation and positive coorientation give TF its orientation. Since the positive normals point inward on every C_i, the boundary orientation of W is the same negative of this leaf orientation on every component. The finite tangent zero-count/inward-boundary-sum lemma constructs a generic rank2 section over W with oriented1-dimensional zero set and gives directly 0=−Σ_i χ(C_i). Its finite surface index count is V−E+F. No general Thom existence, 3D finite CW construction or unproved e_fin comparison is needed.

No C_i is a sphere. A compact spherical leaf would invoke the supplied C² global spherical stability theorem and force every leaf spherical, making L spherical and met by a closed transversal (or the whole foliation a sphere fibration), contrary to L’s no-transversal property and its nonzero Π class in the application. By the supplied finite oriented compact-surface normal form, all remaining C_i have χ(C_i)≤0. Their finite sum is0, so each χ(C_i)=0 and each is diffeomorphic to T². Since L is one of these boundary leaves, the ORIGINAL L is a torus. This obtains torus identification without first assuming that the Π-side accessibility class has sole boundary L. It does not assert that W itself is a solid torus.

proposed_local_additions.statement: For a fixed-V fence with every positive loop null and simple in its leaf universal cover, and with the sphere-cover alternative excluded, the canonical based Jordan caps form a Hausdorff C² disk bundle over (0,b]. Its evaluation admits coherent regular C² cap development with V-orbit tracks over all positive parameters. If its zero loop is essential, at least one material point has infinite normal clock.
proposed_local_additions.title: Canonical Jordan cap development and an infinite normal clock
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
For t>0 choose the universal cover of its leaf based at the fence basepoint, and lift the entire null loop from that point. Its lift is simple. The surface-Jordan disk supplier gives the unique compact disk region Δ_t bounded by this lift; uniqueness uses that the universal cover is not a sphere. The sphere alternative is excluded by the separately supplied compact spherical-leaf global stability carrier: such a leaf forces the foliation to have only spherical leaves, whereas the initial loop is essential. Include the based coverpoint, not only its projected image, in Δ_t. Define E as the disjoint union of these Δ_t, with projection π to t.

At a fixed r>0 transport the compact cap over a small two-sided interval using finitely many foliation boxes and fixed-V roots. This yields a regular cap at every nearby t, with exactly the prescribed boundary word by transport uniqueness. Lift it from the prescribed basepoint to the universal cover of its leaf. A regular lifted disk map with simple boundary is a diffeomorphism onto the unique Jordan region: it is a local diffeomorphism; its degree across the boundary is ±1, and all local degrees have the same sign, so every point inside has exactly one preimage and every point outside none. The degree count follows by finite triangulation of the compact parameter disk and cancellation of internal oriented edges, so does not require a global uniformization theorem. Therefore the transported caps identify D²×J_r with E over J_r. If two such charts overlap, both identify each fiber with exactly the same based Jordan region. Their transition map is the inverse of one regular leafwise parametrization composed with the other. Locally this inverse is C² by the plaque inverse function theorem; uniqueness of the based lift fixes which local branch is used. Cover the compact common disk fiber by finitely many such branches to obtain a C² transition on a smaller overlap. The transition maps satisfy the cocycle identity because they identify actual based coverpoints, not arbitrarily chosen parametrizations.

These charts define a locally trivial Hausdorff C² disk bundle. For different base parameters disjoint base intervals separate points. For points in one fiber, one common product chart separates them by disjoint disk neighborhoods. Thus E is Hausdorff. Its projection is proper over compact parameter bands: shrink a finite cover of a compact band K by trivializing intervals to finitely many closed compact sets K_i inside those intervals; π^{-1}(K_i) is K_i×D² and compact, and their finite union is π^{-1}(K). The evaluation e:E→M is C² and a local diffeomorphism in the interior, because it has two independent plaque directions and one transverse direction. It may have multiple sheets; E retains their based coverpoints.

Lift the one fixed ambient field V through these local inverse branches, giving a C¹ field W on E. On overlaps the branches agree by the identified coverpoints, so W is globally defined. Along ∂E it is tangent to ∂E because the boundary fence tracks are V-orbits. Its π-component has one strict sign. After choosing that sign positive, normalize to W/(dπ(W)), so its base parameter has derivative1. On a compact positive band properness gives a compact total space, a positive minimum for dπ(W), and bounded local fields. The usual finite-chart ODE extension argument therefore transports the entire compact reference disk across the whole band; no interior solution can escape through the boundary because W is tangent there. Exhausting the positive interval by compact bands and using uniqueness gives coherent disk transport from the reference fiber at b to every t>0. Locally this transport is C²: a point is evaluated along a smooth V-flow from a C² cap chart, and the hitting time of a prescribed nearby plaque is the unique root of a C² scalar equation with nonzero derivative. The C² implicit function theorem gives the joint root and cap map. This uses the special transverse-root construction, not a false generic assertion that a C¹ vector field has a C² flow. The resulting evaluation G:D²×(0,b]→M is regular, has the specified boundary fence, and its point tracks follow V-orbits with possibly parameter-dependent speed.

Choose a C¹ defining form ω for the cooriented foliation and a smooth positive transverse field V on compact M, with ω(V)≥c>0. Such data are built by finite chart bumps. Let Φ be its smooth complete ambient flow and B=G_b the compact reference cap. Since D_xG_t is tangent to the foliation, differentiation gives 0=ω(DΦ_{−τ}D_xB)−ω(V)D_xτ, hence |D_xτ|≤C(T) whenever 0≤τ≤T. Indeed DΦ_s and DB are uniformly bounded for |s|≤T on the compact reference domain and compact M, and the denominator is ≥c. This is a bound in the fixed Euclidean disk domain, not an unsupported uniform leaf metric assertion.

If τ₀(x)=lim_{t↓0}τ(x,t) is finite, choose T>τ₀(x)+2δ with δ>0. For y joined to x inside D² by a path of length less than δ/C(T), τ(y,t) cannot reach T: at its first crossing of T along the path, the derivative bound up to that crossing would give T−τ(x,t)<δ, contrary to τ(x,t)≤τ₀(x)<T−2δ. Thus a fixed neighborhood of x has all clocks uniformly bounded by T. The same derivative bound gives local uniform Lipschitz control and makes τ₀ locally continuous wherever all clocks are finite in that neighborhood.

Suppose every clock is finite. The preceding neighborhoods cover compact D², so a finite subcover yields one global bound T for all x and t. The derivative formula then gives global equicontinuity. The monotone pointwise limits τ₀ are continuous and convergence is uniform: take a finite sufficiently fine disk net, obtain uniform convergence at its finitely many points, and use the common Lipschitz bound to control the remaining points. Therefore G_t converges uniformly to the continuous map G₀(x)=Φ_{−τ₀(x)}B(x).

This limit is intrinsically leafwise without a differentiability assumption. Around any x choose a small connected disk patch whose G₀ image lies in one foliation box; uniform convergence puts its G_t images in that box for small t. Each such G_t patch has constant transverse box coordinate, because it is connected and leafwise tangent. Passing to the limit gives constant transverse coordinate on the G₀ patch. Thus G₀ locally maps continuously into one plaque. Connectedness of D² makes all patches belong to one leaf, and its boundary is γ in the original leaf, so this leaf is the original one. Hence G₀ is a continuous intrinsic leafwise null cap for γ, contradicting essentiality. Some clock is therefore infinite. Only continuity of finite-clock limits is used; no unproved C² endpoint map or derivative convergence is invoked.

proposed_local_additions.statement: On the original compact torus leaf, a nonzero Π^j class has a primitive embedded representative with the same Π^j property; its sufficiently short fixed-flow fence is an embedded annulus and each positive boundary bounds an actual embedded disk in its leaf.
proposed_local_additions.title: A torus Π class has a primitive embedded Π root
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Identify π₁(L)=Z² through the supplied torus normal form. Write the nonzero class α=mβ with m≥1 and β=(p,q) primitive, gcd(|p|,|q|)=1. The straight segment in R² from0 to(p,q) projects to an embedded torus loop g: if two interior parameter values had equal projections, their difference times(p,q) would be an integer pair, and Bezout’s identity would make that difference an integer, impossible between0 and1. Compact based homotopy transport identifies the original α fence loops with the m-fold loop of the g fence.

Let h be g’s increasing one-sided holonomy. Since α has identity one-sided holonomy, h^m(t)=t for every sufficiently small positive t. An increasing map has no nontrivial finite orbit: if h(t)>t then its successive iterates strictly increase, while if h(t)<t they strictly decrease. Thus h(t)=t, and the short displaced loops g_t close. Their m-fold loops are null by the transported compact homotopy and α’s Π property. Oriented-surface fundamental groups are torsion-free, so [g_t]^m=1 implies [g_t]=1. The original β is nonzero, giving a genuine embedded Π cycle on the same original leaf and chosen side.

Use the one fixed transverse flow to construct g’s fence F(u,t)=Φ_{τ(u,t)}g(u), with τ_t>0. Short compact-leafwise separation for g(S¹) gives injectivity of the FULL annulus: if F(u,t)=F(v,s), flow uniqueness gives Φ_{τ(u,t)−τ(v,s)}g(u)=g(v), so separation forces equality of times and of g(u),g(v). Embeddedness of g yields u=v, and strict τ_t yields t=s. Compact-to-Hausdorff then makes the fence an embedding. In particular every g_t is an embedded null curve in its actual leaf. The supplied surface-Jordan disk lemma in the leaf, rather than only in its universal cover, gives an actual embedded disk bounded by g_t. The spherical-leaf alternative is excluded as before, ensuring the selected disk is unique. This is the legitimate stronger input for the embedded Reeb construction, not a deduction of ambient cap embedding from the earlier simple universal-cover caps.

proposed_local_additions.statement: Let G:D²×[a,b]→M be a C² immersed disk sweep, transverse in the time direction with one constant sign. Suppose an interior subdisk U⊂D² at the b-base is identified to the whole a-base by a diffeomorphism h:D²→U satisfying G(y,a)=G(h(y),b), with their leafwise tangent maps agreeing under h. On the quotient X, the induced map is locally open at every interior seam point; its compact image has boundary contained in the image of ∂X. No global injectivity is required.
proposed_local_additions.title: Paired cap sweeps are locally open across their seams
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
At a seam point choose a small leafwise plaque chart around its common image. The a-base and b-base maps have invertible leafwise differentials, so after shrinking each has a plaque inverse branch and its nearby time slices are graphs over that plaque patch. The differential in the time direction has the same nonzero transverse sign on both sheets. The piece of the cylinder adjoining the a-base has parameter t>a, whereas the piece adjoining the b-base has t<b. Therefore their transverse graph coordinates occupy opposite sides of the common base plaque, with uniform nonzero first derivative after shrinking. Each half supplies a local half-neighborhood of that plaque; their union supplies a full neighborhood. The leafwise identification h pairs the base inverse branches, so this is precisely a neighborhood of the seam point in X. Away from the seams, G is an ordinary local diffeomorphism by its two leafwise directions and transverse time direction. Thus every interior point of X has image locally open. Because X is compact and M Hausdorff, the image f(X) is closed. If z∈f(X) is not in f(∂X), each preimage is interior and any one gives a neighborhood of z contained in f(X); hence z is not a boundary point. Therefore ∂f(X)⊂f(∂X). This argument allows multiple image sheets and does not substitute immersion for an embedding.

On the unglued b-base annulus D²\U, the available cylinder side is t<b; if G_t is negatively transverse, that is the positive transverse side. Hence at each regular annulus point the positive transverse direction points inward to the locally occupied image side. A no-exit argument must separately control the lateral fence and possible multiple boundary sheets; the present lemma proves seam openness and image-boundary containment only.

proposed_local_additions.statement: Let γ be an essential original loop and γ_t its short fixed-flow null fence boundaries. Every Jordan lifted disk cap of γ_t has projected image disjoint from γ and from one fixed intrinsic neighborhood of γ in its original leaf.
proposed_local_additions.title: Jordan lifted caps avoid the original essential loop
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
First split cases. If the reduced original leaf A is compact, shrink its positive fence using compact separation for K=A, so its positive boundaries and entire cap leaves are distinct from A. Every cap then misses the ENTIRE A, and uniform neighborhood avoidance is automatic. If A is noncompact, its torsion-free group follows from the compact-subspace-with-nonempty-boundary/free-word argument in the finite surface adapter. In that case use the following deck proof. Short fixed-flow separation for K=γ(S¹) makes every boundary γ_t disjoint from γ. If a projected disk met γ, its leaf would be the original leaf L. Lift the crossing to the disk in the universal cover of L. The lift of γ through it stays in the disk, because it cannot cross the disk boundary (its projection is disjoint from γ_t). The next lift of γ, starting at its endpoint, also stays in the disk; inductively the whole orbit under the nonidentity deck element α represented by γ lies in the compact lifted disk. Proper discontinuity of the deck action permits only finitely many orbit points in a compact set. Thus α has finite order, contrary to torsion-freeness of the oriented surface group. Hence the projected cap misses γ.

Choose a relatively compact intrinsic neighborhood S of γ in L and a smaller connected-near-γ neighborhood S′ with closure contained in S, so every point of S′ can be joined to γ by a path in S (finite leaf charts suffice). Compact flow separation for closure(S), not merely for γ, ensures every short γ_t avoids S. If a projected cap on L met S′, lift a path in S from that point to γ starting inside the lifted disk. It cannot leave the disk: crossing its boundary would project to an intersection of γ_t with S. Its endpoint therefore lies inside the disk and projects to γ, contradicting the first part. Thus all these cap images avoid S′ uniformly. Other-leaf caps are automatically disjoint from S′. This proof corrects the source’s unsupported uniform intrinsic-distance assertion by applying compact separation to an enlarged intrinsic compact neighborhood.

proposed_local_additions.statement: On the original Π torus, choose its primitive Π meridian β and a complementary longitude λ. Its one-sided longitude holonomy can be chosen strictly contracting. The collar longitude annuli grow the actual meridian caps, and their iterates exhaust each nearby leaf as a plane with limit set exactly the original torus. The limit set means ambient limits of sequences escaping every intrinsic compact subset of the leaf, equivalently the intersection of closures of tails of a cofinal compact exhaustion.
proposed_local_additions.title: A contracting longitude exhausts the nearby plane leaves
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
The meridian β has identity one-sided holonomy. Let H be the increasing longitude holonomy on a common small transversal. If H(t)=t at any sufficiently small positive t, β and λ both fix t, and the finite-generator graph lemma produces a compact one-sheeted nearby leaf. Its meridian is essential by collar projection, contradicting the Π meridian’s displaced nullness. Therefore H has no positive fixed point on one small connected interval. Replace λ by its inverse if necessary so 0<H(t)<t. Its iterates decrease to0, since their limit would otherwise be a positive fixed point.

Finite plaque transport over a cut fundamental polygon of the torus gives the actual collar suspension: β identifies the meridian edges without a transverse change and λ identifies the longitude edges by H. This construction uses finitely many compact chart relations, all valid after one common shrink. For each t the longitude circuit, thickened by the meridian coordinate, gives an embedded leafwise annulus A_t from β_t to β_H(t); its base projection travels once over the complementary torus annulus. Two disjoint embedded null circles in a nonspherical oriented leaf joined by an annulus have nested Jordan disks, and their disk difference is that annulus. Otherwise the two disks and annulus would form an open-and-closed sphere leaf. The nesting direction is locally constant in t by compact cap transport and the disjoint boundary circles. It cannot be shrinking: if D_H(t)⊂D_t, iteration would place every β_H^n(t) inside the compact D_t, but these circles approach the original torus, which is disjoint from D_t; the positive ambient distance of these two compact sets gives a contradiction. Hence D_H(t)=D_t∪A_t for every small t.

The union of increasing D_H^n(t) is the ENTIRE nearby leaf. Given any point of that leaf, join it to a point in D_t by a compact intrinsic path. Its ambient image is compact and disjoint from the original compact torus, hence has positive distance from it. Late boundary circles β_H^n(t) lie arbitrarily close to the torus and avoid that path. Starting inside the late disk, the path cannot leave it without crossing its boundary, so its endpoint belongs to the disk. An increasing union of disks with each compactly inside the next is a plane: choose successive disk/annulus homeomorphisms to concentric disks of radii n and glue them; the exact differences A_H^n(t) provide the required annuli. These annuli lie in collar heights tending uniformly to0. They therefore have no limit points away from the original torus; every point of that torus is approached, because their meridian/longitude base projections cover the entire torus. The compact initial disk contributes no intrinsic end-limit points. Thus the leaf limit set is exactly the original torus.

This limit-set convention is independent of the chosen exhaustion: any intrinsic compact subset is contained in a sufficiently late disk because those disks form an increasing open cover, and compactness selects finitely many whose maximum contains it. Thus the disk exhaustion is cofinal among intrinsic compact sets. Intersection of closed exhaustion tails and the escaping-sequence definition agree in the compact metric ambient space by choosing one point from each shrinking rational neighborhood and tail, using ACω. The annular tails approach L uniformly, while their torus base projections cover it, proving exactly L for that convention.

proposed_local_additions.statement: Suppose the cap family has an infinite negative-transverse center trajectory q(s), synchronized parameters t(s)↓0, and the preceding fixed-neighborhood avoidance. Then after adjusting recurrence times there is one leaf B and one fixed plaque patch in B whose lifts lie in the interiors of all sufficiently late caps.
proposed_local_additions.title: Infinite cap tracks give actual common-plaque recurrence
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Compactness of M and countable choice give an accumulation point z of q(s) for s→∞. Choose a small box around z where the transverse derivative of the fixed negative flow has a uniform nonzero bound. If q(s_n)→z, adjust each s_n by a time tending to0 so q(s_n) lies on the central plaque through z: solve the strictly monotone transverse-coordinate equation by the intermediate value theorem. The infinite trajectory permits both small time directions once s_n is large. These adjusted points all lie in the same leaf B.

The accumulation point z cannot lie on γ. Otherwise choose the box in the intrinsic neighborhood S′ of the original leaf provided by the avoidance lemma. The same small time adjustment places q(s_n) on its central original-leaf plaque inside S′, contradicting that q(s_n) is in the interior of a cap. Thus z∉γ(S¹). A fixed smaller box about z has closure disjoint from γ, and every late boundary γ_{t(s_n)} avoids that box by uniform convergence to γ. Each adjusted cap-center is interior to its Jordan lifted disk. In the lifted central plaque rectangle containing that center, disk-interior membership cannot change along a path without crossing the disk boundary. Since the entire projected rectangle is boundary-free and connected, it lies inside the lifted disk. Shrink to a fixed smaller rectangle around z and take n sufficiently large that the adjusted center belongs to it. This gives one common intrinsic plaque patch in B, with its lift based at a fixed point of that patch in every cap. The argument concerns actual central-plaque hits, rather than replacing ambient convergence by an assertion that the convergent points already share a leaf.

proposed_local_additions.statement: For recurrent caps with simple universal-cover boundaries and a common interior plaque patch, one can choose an increasing sequence of source-disk inclusions whose projected cap maps agree on the included disks, even if the projected caps are immersed.
proposed_local_additions.title: Recurrent caps have nested source-disk inclusions
proposed_local_additions.strategy: Fix a late cap C_n. Its projected image is compact and is disjoint from the original γ by the avoidance lemma. The compact sets image(C_n) and γ(S¹) are disjoint in a metric ambient manifold, so have positive distance. Uniform convergence γ_t→γ therefore implies that every sufficiently late boundary γ_{t(s_m)} avoids the entire projected image(C_n). Base both lifted caps in the universal cover of B at the same point of their common plaque patch. Their Jordan disk regions Δ_n and Δ_m overlap there, and ∂Δ_m is disjoint from Δ_n because its projection avoids image(C_n). Any path in the connected disk Δ_n from the common interior point to another point cannot exit Δ_m without crossing ∂Δ_m. Hence Δ_n⊂int(Δ_m). proposed_local_additions.title: The primitive cap block embeds as the standard Reeb component
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Fix a small e and sweep the actual caps over [H(e),e]. Since D_H(e)=D_e∪A_e, identify the whole e-base with its included source disk in the H(e)-base. The quotient X is a solid torus: the disk cylinder is a 3-ball, and identifying two disjoint boundary disks is the attachment of one 1-handle; disk collars explicitly convert this quotient to D²×S¹. The preceding seam charts give a local homeomorphism, piecewise C² and orientation coherent, at every interior point. Its boundary map is an EMBEDDED torus C: the lateral meridian fence is embedded; the unglued base annulus maps to A_e; their interiors are disjoint in the finite collar suspension and they meet only at their two boundary meridians. It is a collar graph over the original torus, with corners removable by local rounding.

Prove global injectivity by preimage counts. For y outside C the finite number n(y) of interior preimages is locally constant: compactness and local injectivity make the fiber finite, finite inverse neighborhoods cover all its points, and the image of their compact complement excludes a small target neighborhood. Every positive cap leaf differs from the original torus, so the whole cap-block image misses that torus. Thus n=0 on the component of M\C containing it. Across C the count changes by exactly1, because its boundary has exactly one preimage and a half-chart; any interior preimages would contribute the same positive count on both sides. Consequently C separates, n=1 on its other component, and C has no interior preimages (one would give positive count on the zero side). There are at most two complement components: both collar sides of connected C are connected, and each complementary component has boundary in C. Hence X maps bijectively onto the closure of the nonzero side. It is a homeomorphism by compactness, and a C² diffeomorphism in the manifold charts after rounding. Attach the product collar between C and the original torus L. This yields a compact solid torus R with boundary exactly L. Since L is a leaf, an ambient leaf cannot cross it; every point in R belongs to one of the cap/annulus leaves, so R is saturated. The previous exhaustion proves that all its interior leaves are planes and their limit set is L.

For the foliated model choose an increasing interval conjugacy ψ with ψ(H(t))=qψ(t), q=1/2. Pick any increasing homeomorphism of [H(e),e] to [qe′,e′], extend over H-iterates by the equation, and put ψ(0)=0. Endpoints match, monotone iterates tend to0, and the inverse construction gives a continuous inverse. In the finite torus suspension collar the map (meridian u, longitude s, transverse t)↦(u,s,ψ(t)) respects the longitude identifications, so it is a foliated homeomorphism to the standard contracting collar. Identify the fundamental cap disks at the two ends with the standard disks, using the exact annulus A_e to make their boundary identifications match. Extend these endpoint disk maps continuously across the compact parameter block: circle boundary maps interpolate by their increasing angle lifts, and disk maps fixing their boundary interpolate by the Alexander radial isotopy; equivalently triangulate the finitely many disk/annulus collars and extend their matching boundary maps cellwise. Choose the endpoint compatibility χ_H(e)∘h=h_std∘χ_e, where h is the included source disk map. Then the product cap maps descend over the paired bases and glue exactly to the collar map. They send every disk/annulus leaf to its standard counterpart, giving a bijective foliated map on the whole interior.

At L the map has the fixed torus base-coordinate map. Any points approaching L eventually lie in an arbitrarily thin compact torus collar, and ψ(t)→0 uniformly in its bounded base coordinates; hence their images approach the corresponding boundary points. Conversely ψ^{-1}(t)→0 gives the same uniform statement for inverse images. Away from L all maps are product/chart homeomorphisms. Thus the global map and inverse are continuous everywhere, including the limiting boundary. This proves the standard Reeb foliated homeomorphism; it asserts no smooth conjugacy of arbitrary contracting germs.

For the disk-map extension, define χ_H(e) on the included disk h(D²) by h_std∘χ_e∘h^{-1}, and define it on its actual complementary annulus by the already specified suspension-collar map. The maps agree on the common meridian. Boundary circle homeomorphisms have increasing angle lifts a(θ+2π)=a(θ)+2π; convex interpolation of two such lifts remains increasing and defines continuous circle maps and inverses. proposed_local_additions.title: An immersed paired cap sweep excludes closed transversals
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
The intersections of the original transversal with K are isolated: in a foliation box the transversal has strictly monotone transverse coordinate while each local K branch lies in a plaque. Compactness and finitely many local branches give finitely many intersections, after first a small positive perturbation if necessary to avoid passage through double points of K. Choose disjoint parameter intervals for all intersections other than p and small boxes where each K branch is an embedded arc in one plaque. In box coordinates replace the transversal by a small tangentially shifted arc near its crossing, interpolating to the original arc on end collars. Choose the tangential shift transverse to the one-dimensional branch in the two-dimensional plaque. It misses that branch; the transverse-coordinate derivative stays positive because the shift changes only tangential coordinates. Shrink each box to exclude all other K branches or, at a doublepoint, select a shift avoiding both of the finitely many arcs. The interpolation occurs at transverse levels separated from the branch plaque, so introduces no new intersections. Finite gluing retains C² regularity and positivity. At p keep an interval fixed. The remainder outside a slightly larger p-box is compact and disjoint from K, hence has positive ambient metric distance from K. This last uniform-distance assertion applies only after fixing that box and transversal, not to an arbitrary varying family.

Choose a small box B around the regular initial point p so the initial loop meets B in one embedded arc, with every other boundary parameter outside a larger closed box. Uniform continuity of the short fence keeps those other parameters outside B at all sufficiently small levels. In each plaque met by the boundary, its sole boundary arc is C¹ close to the initial regular arc. A fixed smaller plaque rectangle is therefore split into two connected half-rectangles by this arc, with one uniform tangential and normal size. Lift B to the universal cover of the leaf at that boundary point; the component of the plaque rectangle through the chosen lift maps diffeomorphically to its plaque rectangle. The Jordan boundary has no other boundary points in this lifted rectangle, because all other projected boundary parameters avoid B. Its disk side contains one local half-neighborhood by the boundary collar. Membership in the Jordan interior cannot change along a path in the corresponding half-rectangle without crossing the boundary. Thus the entire chosen half-rectangle lies in the disk. This is inclusion of a local plaque patch, and does not treat the globally projected disk as embedded. Leaf orientation identifies the selected side with the sign of the boundary orientation; on any connected interval with compact cap transport that sign is constant. If global regular cap continuation is unavailable, constancy on the entire interval must be supplied separately.

Suppose a positive closed transversal meets the reduced initial leaf. Finite leaf-path transport and positive perturbation move a crossing to a regular point p of the essential loop γ, away from its finitely many double points. Tangential perturbations in finitely many foliation boxes remove its other intersections with γ, as in the transversal-avoidance lemma. In a fixed-V flowbox near p write coordinates (x,z), with V-orbits vertical and γ an embedded arc in z=0. Replace the local transversal, preserving its positive transverse derivative and its end collars, by τ(r)=(p+r v,r) near r=0, where v is a small vector pointing into the selected local cap half-plaque. For r≠0 sufficiently small its basepoint lies off γ. Since the whole normal fence is made of V-orbits over γ, this local transversal misses the ENTIRE positive fence; the compact remainder of τ has positive distance from γ, so after shrinking the fence it also misses the fence. Hence τ is disjoint from the entire lateral boundary A₀ of every sufficiently late paired sweep.

Fix a late upper cap C_n and its compact projected image, disjoint from γ. Choose the lower recurrent cap C_m sufficiently late that C_n is included in it by the source-disk inclusion h_{n,m}, and that a fixed small neighborhood of p disjoint from image(C_n) contains γ_{t_m} near p. In that box the cap C_m contains the uniform local plaque half-neighborhood from the half-plaque lemma. The local leaf plaque is a graph z=η_m(x) with η_m(p)>0 and tending to0; transversality and small v make r−η_m(p+r v) strictly increasing. It has a small positive zero r_m. At this point τ crosses the C_m plaque on its selected interior side because its tangential displacement r_m v is inward. The crossing lies outside image(C_n), so it belongs to the unglued b-base annulus A₁. Thus τ meets f(A₁), and misses f(A₀) and their boundary seams.

The paired quotient X is an oriented compact 3-manifold with boundary A₀∪A₁: identifying the whole a-base disk to the interior source disk h_{n,m}(D²) of the b-base identifies two boundary disks of the original 3-ball. Local disk collars give manifold charts across the identified bases; its boundary is the remaining b-base annulus and the lateral annulus. The seam lemma strengthens to a local orientation-preserving homeomorphism in the interior: the two half-charts map injectively to opposite sides of their common plaque and agree on that plaque. Other interior charts are regular local diffeomorphisms. Along A₁ the positive transverse direction points inward to X, since this b-base has available cylinder side t<b and the sweep is negatively transverse.

Form the fiber product P={(x,r)∈X×S¹:f(x)=τ(r)}. It is closed in the compact product, hence compact. Interior local homeomorphism charts of f identify P locally with an interval of the oriented transversal; the piecewise C² seam causes no topological defect. Along A₁ transversality gives half-interval charts. There are no points over A₀ or the boundary corners because τ misses their images. Therefore P is a compact oriented 1-manifold with boundary. Its boundary is nonempty by the crossing above. At every boundary point the positive τ direction enters X, so every boundary point has the same boundary sign. This is impossible: a compact oriented 1-manifold has zero total signed boundary. To see this without an imported classification theorem, choose a finite oriented interval-chart cover, subdivide the compact 1-manifold into finitely many short intervals subordinate to it, and cancel paired internal endpoints; each interval contributes one positive and one negative endpoint. Contradiction. Thus the reduced leaf meets no closed positive transversal. This uses multiple-sheet preimages with their multiplicities and never identifies an immersed cap image with an embedded region.

proposed_local_additions.title: A recurrent Π-side leaf gives a distinct accessibility boundary
proposed_local_additions.strategy:
Use a sufficiently small compact-leaf collar and the nearby compact-leaf graph lemma. Any compact leaf through a positive base parameter t would be a one-sheeted graph over L and would make the transported original essential Π loop essential, contrary to its nullness. Hence every sufficiently near positive Π-side leaf is intrinsically noncompact. The recurrent common-plaque leaf B meets infinitely many positive base parameters t_n↓0, since the cap boundaries on that same leaf include the specified fence basepoints. It is one of these noncompact leaves. By the intrinsic-noncompact-leaf transversal lemma, B meets a positive closed immersed transversal.

Let S be B’s mutual-positive-accessibility class. It is saturated by definition. It is open: the closed transversal gives a strict positive return from B to itself. Finite box transport and small endpoint perturbations of its crossing give strict positive paths from B to every leaf through a small neighborhood of a crossing, and back from each such leaf to B (start and end the loop on opposite sides of the perturbed crossing). These leaves lie in S. Transporting these open crossing neighborhoods along any finite leafwise path gives openness at every point of every leaf in S; for another leaf in S concatenate its strict paths to and from B with the same perturbed return construction. No formal reflexive relation is substituted for a strict positive return.

S is disjoint from L. If L belonged to S, the strict paths L→B and B→L (distinct leaves) would produce a positive closed transversal meeting L after finite plaque-path endpoint alignment and positive corner smoothing. This contradicts the no-transversal conclusion for L. On the other hand the basepoints of the recurrent cap boundaries lie in B⊂S and converge to the original basepoint x∈L, so x∈closure(S). The closure of a saturated set is saturated: in a box its leafwise plaque projection preserves membership of nearby saturation, and a finite chain of such boxes along a leaf carries any accumulation at one point to accumulation at every other point. Hence L⊂closure(S). Since S is open and disjoint from L, L⊂∂_M S. This is an actual distinct mutual-accessibility component boundary, and uses neither an ordinary complement component nor the unsupplied full closure-manifold classification.

For a compact set K choose finitely many relatively compact surface charts covering it and finitely many C² coordinate bump functions whose sum f exceeds1 on K and has compact support. The union of the components of {f≥a} meeting K is a compact subsurface S with C² boundary and K in its interior; it has finitely many components because its compact regular boundary and compact manifold chart cover give finite component charts. Construct a finite cellulation of S without using arbitrary Jordan curves. Choose finitely many coordinate disks with smaller cores covering S. Move their radii generically so their boundary circles and ∂S intersect transversely, with no triple points; the C² scalar Sard clause on each of the finitely many prior arcs supplies these radii. Add all finitely many crossings as graph vertices. Each arrangement face has constant membership in every disk, hence lies in one disk whose core-cover point it contains. Within that coordinate disk, straighten finite regular arcs near their vertices and replace each compact regular edge by a close polygonal edge inside its disjoint thin strip. Compact inverse-function neighborhoods ensure the replacement is a graph over the old edge, so stripwise interpolation is an ambient isotopy. For an isolated closed regular curve, its short normal collar is injective by compactness and IFT; a sufficiently fine inscribed polygon is a graph in that collar and isotopic to it. Thus only the choice-free polygonal Jordan theorem is required. Add finite planar crosscuts between distinct boundary components of an arrangement face, then triangulate its simple polygonal faces by ears. Reconcile the finite subdivisions on shared edges. Reversing the strip isotopies gives a finite curvilinear triangular cellulation of S. This is the finite supplied-chart part of the published curvilinear construction, with its full-AC arbitrary-Jordan input replaced by the regular-curve polygon argument just given.

Cut a spanning tree of the finite primal graph and a spanning tree of the dual graph to obtain one finite polygon schema (published one-polygon lemma, proof steps1.1–3.1). All orientable paired sides occur with opposite traversal signs. The finite schema moves cancel adjacent aa^{-1}; an interlaced pair a,b is cut and pasted into one handle block aba^{-1}b^{-1}, which is set aside. If no pair interlaces, an innermost adjacent inverse pair exists and cancels. Each operation deletes a pair or sets aside a block, so finite side count decreases. Unpaired boundary circles remain boundary circles. The result is genus g with b boundary circles, χ=2−2g−b; for b>0, the standard polygon edge retraction gives the free group on 2g+b−1 generators. These are the finite operations in the published polygonal reduction-moves item, not its full-AC triangulation-existence premise. For b=0 the same schema gives sphere for g=0, torus for g=1, and the usual oriented genus-g model; χ=0 identifies exactly the torus. Finite regular chart and collar smoothing makes the model maps C² diffeomorphisms in the present C² category.

Torsion-freeness is local to a compact subsurface: a loop and a null cap of its m-th power have compact connected image K, so lie in such an S. With boundary, π₁(S) is free and cyclic reduction of a nonempty reduced word shows its positive powers stay nonempty. For closed S, genus0 has trivial group and genus1 has Z². The boundary word is a nonempty cyclically reduced product of commutators in each free factor, so those edge injections are injective. The published amalgam normal-form theorem then makes any finite-order element conjugate into a factor: an alternating cyclically reduced word has powers of strictly increasing syllable length. Thus no torsion exists. Its coset data require no full AC here: free groups have explicit finite-word enumerations, and one chooses the first word in each cyclic coset.

If it separates and neither side is a disk, their boundary subgroup generated by c injects in each side: the finite polygon word is nonempty in each non-disk oriented boundary surface. Van Kampen and amalgam normal form would then make c nontrivial in S, contradicting the supplied null cap. Hence one side is a disk, embedded in S and therefore in the original surface.
